assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, via the magic-wavelength idea and its realization with strontium, opened a new regime of frequency metrology with stability and accuracy beyond the caesium standard. The discovery is clear, original and has lasting impact on redefinition of the second, relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental physics.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and built the first lattice clock; Ye brought the clock to systematic uncertainties at the 1e-18 level and many-body clock physics. Two laureates give a clean, defensible configuration; other groups (for example Lemonde, Takamoto) are not in the credited names and would need to be considered separately.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by many laboratories worldwide over two decades with steadily improving performance; the interpretation is stable and recognition is timely, if not overdue.
uncertainties: Whether earlier optical-clock work (single-ion clocks, already partly recognized) leaves room for a lattice-clock prize is a matter of judgement.
The allocation between Katori and Ye of the decisive contributions, and exclusion of other contributors, is not fully certain from the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction and observation of the quantum spin Hall state and the resulting concept of topological insulators reshaped condensed-matter physics, linking band topology, spin-orbit coupling and protected edge transport. Originality and breadth of impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical proposal of the Z2 invariant and the quantum spin Hall effect in graphene; Molenkamp led the experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells. Credited names support a theory-plus-experiment prize, though Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and Konig are not in the supplied credit, which I believe is a real attribution complication.
assessment.maturity: Mature: more than fifteen years of confirmation across materials, with surface-state and transport evidence from multiple groups; the field is established, so recognition is on time.
uncertainties: Competing and overlapping contributions (e.g. the HgTe quantum-well proposal and three-dimensional topological insulators) make an equitable three-person configuration contested.
I am relying on my own recollection of the history rather than verified sources.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cold atoms in optical lattices as controllable quantum simulators of Hubbard-type many-body systems, including the superfluid to Mott-insulator transition and quantum gas microscopy, provide a new way of studying strongly correlated matter. The concept is original and influential well beyond atomic physics.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch and others) proposed the Bose-Hubbard realization; Bloch and Greiner realized the Mott transition and single-site resolved imaging. This fits a fair theory-plus-experiment configuration, though Hansch and others made early contributions that are not in the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed by many groups and now an established platform; quantum simulation results of practical advantage over classical methods remain an ongoing question, but the foundational discoveries are mature.
uncertainties: Overlap with the Nobel recognition already given for cold-atom physics (BEC, laser cooling) may be argued either way.
Credit within the Mott-transition work involves more people than three, leaving some allocation uncertainty.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The KPZ equation identified a universality class for non-equilibrium interface growth with exact results (including Tracy-Widom statistics) linking statistical physics, random matrices and integrable probability. Liquid-crystal experiments gave a clean, quantitative confirmation of the full distribution. As a statistical physicist, I regard this as one of the cleanest examples of universality outside equilibrium.
assessment.attribution: Kardar, Parisi and Zhang wrote the 1986 equation; here Parisi is not among the credited names (and he already holds a prize), so the supplied credit leaves out an original author, which weakens the case. Takeuchi supplied the decisive experimental confirmation. Exact solutions were provided by mathematicians and theorists (Johansson, Prahofer-Spohn, Sasamoto-Spohn, Amir-Corwin-Quastel) who are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Theory is firmly established; the experimental confirmation is clear and has been reproduced in other systems, but the extent of KPZ universality in real growth settings is still debated.
uncertainties: The credit for the original equation is incomplete, and the exact-solution contributions are spread among many people.
Whether the committee would view this as sufficiently broad in impact is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Vicsek model and the Toner-Tu hydrodynamic theory showed that collective motion has genuine long-range order in two dimensions, in contrast with equilibrium systems (Mermin-Wagner), and founded the field of active matter. This is original and conceptually clear; the impact on soft matter, biology and complex systems is broad.
assessment.attribution: Vicsek and colleagues introduced the minimal model; Toner and Tu developed the continuum theory and renormalization-group results. The credit is reasonably clear for the three names, although Ramaswamy, Marchetti and others are significant contributors to later active-matter theory.
assessment.maturity: Theory is highly developed with many numerical and experimental tests (bacteria, colloids, bird flocks), but quantitative confirmation of the specific scaling exponents in experiments is less secure, so maturity is moderate.
uncertainties: Experimental verification of Toner-Tu exponents is limited and often indirect.
Parisi's 2021 prize recognized complex-systems physics, which may affect the committee's appetite for another such prize so soon.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Conformal field theory of two-dimensional critical phenomena gave exact critical exponents and a complete classification of universality classes in two dimensions, with deep reach into string theory and statistical mechanics. This is among the major theoretical achievements of the late twentieth century.
assessment.attribution: The 1984 paper by Belavin, Polyakov and Zamolodchikov is the decisive source, which supports a clean three-person prize. Contributions of Friedan, Qiu, Shenker, Cardy, Dotsenko and Fateev are not in the supplied credit and would have to be considered; I recall the history of this field imperfectly.
assessment.maturity: The theory is decades old and verified in many lattice models and exact solutions, so maturity is complete; a prize is arguably overdue, but experimental confirmation is indirect.
uncertainties: Several potentially deserving contributors and the status of one credited laureate (I am uncertain about the living status of all three) could prevent a viable configuration.
Mathematical-physics character of the work may fall between physics and mathematics prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BB84 and Ekert's entanglement-based protocol created quantum cryptography, with provable security rooted in quantum mechanics, and relate closely to teleportation. The work is original and has strong societal and technological impact.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard introduced BB84 and Ekert the entanglement-based E91; this is a natural three-person configuration, although the 2022 prize on entanglement has already recognized related foundations.
assessment.maturity: Mature in principle, with commercial and satellite demonstrations from many groups; practical-security issues (side channels) remain active, but the core protocols are well established.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize on entangled photons and quantum information could count against recognition.
Whether practical deployments rather than the protocols should be weighed more heavily is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pulsar timing arrays have produced evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background, opening a new band for gravitational-wave astronomy and probing supermassive black-hole binaries or new physics.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread over several collaborations (NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA, CPTA, InPTA) and many people; the supplied names can support at most three, which does not map cleanly to a fair prize.
assessment.maturity: Premature: the 2023 evidence is at roughly 3-4 sigma for the Hellings-Downs correlation, with the source (supermassive binaries versus other) still unresolved. Further data releases are needed before it is mature.
uncertainties: Significance and astrophysical origin are not yet settled.
Attribution across collaborations is hard to resolve into three individuals.
